topic: Who can hold the Accountable role for an AI decision
stem: In a RACI for a decision produced by an automated Claude-based system, who or what can legitimately hold the Accountable role?

options.text: The AI governance committee as a body, on the basis that it reviewed the system and approved it into production.
The vendor supplying the model, under the indemnity and service terms that cover the deployment in question.
A named individual who can change, pause, or override what the system decides.
The model itself, provided its system card records the decision criteria and the confidence thresholds applied.

explanation.correct: Accountability is the ability to be called to answer and to act on the answer. That requires a person with authority over the thing being governed — someone who can stop it, change it, or override an output. Models have no authority and cannot be sanctioned. Committees can advise, approve and review, but a body that meets monthly cannot be woken at 3am and cannot be held to a decision it collectively made. The accountable role in RACI is singular and human for exactly this reason.

distractors.A: Committees own approval and review, not day-to-day accountability. Diffusing the A across a group is the standard way accountability evaporates: when everyone signed off, no one is answerable, and there is no one with standing to halt the system between meetings.
distractors.B: Contractual recourse against a vendor is a financial remedy, not accountability. The vendor cannot make decisions about how the deploying organisation uses the output, and a regulator or customer will hold the deploying organisation answerable regardless of what the contract says.
distractors.D: A model has no agency, no authority and nothing that can be withdrawn from it. Documenting decision criteria in a system card improves transparency, but transparency about a mechanism is not the same as someone being answerable for the mechanism's effects.

explanation.concept: Accountability attaches to a person with authority to act, never to a system, a model, or a committee. Every AI system in production should map to one named accountable individual who can pause or override it. Responsibility for building, running and reviewing can be shared; the A cannot.
explanation.tip: Any option that puts accountability on a model, a tool, or a standing body is wrong by construction in this domain. Look for the option that names a human with the power to intervene.

topic: Discovering unsanctioned AI use across a large workforce
stem: A Dutch logistics operator with 3,200 staff has been asked by its board for a complete list of AI tools in use. HR circulated a self-declaration form and received twelve declarations. The CISO believes the real figure is far higher. The company issues corporate cards to team leads, runs an identity tenant where third-party application consent is enabled and logged, and retains full egress-proxy records. Which approach produces the most complete picture?

options.text: Re-issue the self-declaration with mandatory line-manager countersignature and a hard deadline, escalating any team that fails to return it to the executive committee for follow-up.

Query the procurement and vendor-master systems for contracts and purchase orders containing AI or machine-learning terms, on the basis that anything material to the business would have passed through purchasing.

Block the well-known consumer AI domains at the egress proxy and treat the helpdesk exception requests that follow as the discovery mechanism, since anyone genuinely dependent on a tool will surface themselves within a week.
Reconcile corporate card and expense line items, third-party application consents in the identity tenant, and egress-proxy destinations against the declared list, then investigate every difference.

explanation.correct: Shadow AI is by definition the use people did not declare, so any method that asks people to declare it inherits the same blind spot. The three data sources named in the stem are the ones the organisation already holds and that record use whether or not anyone reports it: money leaving through cards and expenses, identity grants where staff have connected an AI product to corporate data, and traffic leaving to model-provider endpoints. Reconciling those three against the twelve declarations turns discovery into a difference list that can be worked.

distractors.A: A stronger survey is still a survey. Non-declaration is rarely defiance — it is people not classifying a browser extension or a free tier as an AI tool at all. Adding a countersignature raises the cost of the exercise without touching the reason the first pass missed things.
distractors.B: Procurement records catch only what was purchased centrally. They miss free tiers, personal-card purchases below approval thresholds, trials, browser extensions, and AI capabilities that arrived inside a product the company already bought for another reason.
distractors.C: Blocking generates signal but also generates outage. It surfaces only tools people are willing to argue for, drives the rest onto personal devices where nothing is visible, and damages the trust needed for staff to bring future use forward voluntarily.

explanation.concept: Discover shadow AI from telemetry you already own — spend, identity grants, and network egress — rather than from self-report. Self-declaration works only as a reconciliation step after independent discovery has produced a candidate list to challenge people against.
explanation.tip: When a stem itemises which data sources the organisation has, that list is the answer. Governance items that name card data, consent logs, or proxy records are pointing at reconciliation, not at another questionnaire.

topic: Defining declarable trigger criteria for an AI incident
stem: A Norwegian energy utility runs a Claude assistant that drafts outage notifications to customers. Its incident policy defines an incident in terms of service availability. Over six weeks three things happened: a notification naming the wrong substation went to 4,000 customers; a support agent noticed the assistant citing a decommissioned safety procedure and mentioned it in a team channel; and the assistant was unreachable for twenty minutes. Only the twenty-minute outage was raised as an incident. The risk committee asks how the incident definition should change. Which TWO changes address the gap? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Add trigger criteria based on incorrect or harmful output reaching a customer or being relied on for a decision, independent of whether the service was available.
Require an AI incident to be declared only once the model provider has confirmed a defect, so the utility does not raise incidents for ordinary probabilistic variation in a generative system.
Give any employee a low-friction route to declare a suspected AI incident, with triage assigning severity afterwards rather than requiring the reporter to establish impact first.
Collapse the severity scale into a single AI incident category so that every AI event receives an identical response and no triage judgement is required at declaration time.
Route AI-related events to the monthly model governance forum instead of the incident process, on the basis that generative output problems are quality defects rather than operational failures.

explanation.correct: Both failures the utility missed were failures of output, not of uptime, and an availability-based definition cannot see them. Adding output-harm triggers makes the wrong-substation notification declarable on its face. The decommissioned-procedure case failed differently: someone did notice, but the only route available was a team channel, so the observation never entered the process. A declaration path that any employee can use, with severity decided by triage rather than by the reporter, closes that second gap. A definition that catches the event but has no usable front door still produces zero incidents.

distractors.B: This makes an external party the gatekeeper of the utility's own incident process and misframes the harm. The wrong substation reached customers regardless of whether the model behaved within its expected distribution; the utility owns that outcome and must be able to declare it without waiting on anyone.
distractors.D: Removing severity does not remove judgement, it removes proportionality. Treating a twenty-minute outage and a mass mis-notification identically either over-mobilises the organisation for trivia or, more commonly, causes the whole category to be quietly ignored.
distractors.E: A monthly forum cannot contain an event that is actively reaching customers. Governance forums exist to review patterns and approve changes; diverting live harm into a review agenda guarantees the response is measured in weeks.

explanation.concept: An AI incident definition must be written against outcomes — wrong, harmful, or unsafe output that reached someone or drove a decision — not against availability. Pair the definition with a declaration route that costs the reporter almost nothing and puts the burden of assessing impact on triage.
explanation.tip: When a stem shows that someone noticed a problem and nothing happened, the missing control is the reporting path, not the detection. Two distinct failures in a stem usually mean two distinct keys.

topic: What a system card must add to provider documentation
stem: A German medical-device manufacturer's after-sales function has built a Claude assistant that helps field engineers diagnose equipment faults. The internal standard requires a system card before production. The team submitted the model provider's published model documentation, arguing that capabilities and limitations are already described there. The governance office rejected the submission. What must the system card supply that the provider's documentation cannot?

options.text: A restatement of the provider's published benchmark results, mapped onto the manufacturer's product families so that reviewers can compare the chosen model against the alternatives considered.
The specifics of this deployment: the tasks it is approved for, the data it can reach, results from evaluation against the manufacturer's own fault cases, and the named owner.
The underlying model's training-data composition and architecture, which the provider summarises at a high level but does not disclose to the depth a governance card requires.
A signed attestation from the model provider confirming that the model is fit for diagnostic support in a regulated medical-device setting, countersigned by the manufacturer's quality function.

explanation.correct: Provider documentation describes a model in the abstract. Risk lives in the deployment: which faults this assistant is allowed to opine on, which manuals and service histories it can retrieve, how it performed against the manufacturer's own historical fault cases, what it is known to get wrong in this domain, and who is answerable when it does. None of that exists anywhere except in the deploying team's own testing. A system card that is a copy of the provider's model documentation contains zero information about the risk the manufacturer is actually taking.

distractors.A: Benchmarks measure general capability on public tasks. They say nothing about performance on this manufacturer's fault taxonomy, and mapping them onto product families creates a false impression of task-specific evidence where none was gathered.
distractors.C: Training-data composition belongs to the model layer and is largely outside the deploying organisation's reach. Demanding it stalls the review on something the team cannot produce while leaving the deployment-specific gaps that actually caused the rejection untouched.
distractors.D: No provider attests to fitness for a specific regulated use, and it would not help if one did. Fitness for this use is a determination the deploying organisation makes from its own evaluation evidence and then owns.

explanation.concept: A model card describes the model; a system card describes what your organisation built with it. The card's value is entirely in the deployment-specific content: approved scope, reachable data, evaluation results on your data, known failure modes in your context, the human oversight step, and the accountable owner.
explanation.tip: If a proposed governance artefact could be produced without ever looking at the team's own system, it is not the artefact being asked for. Watch for teams substituting upstream documentation for their own evidence.

topic: The element that keeps a policy exception register a control
stem: An AI policy exception has been granted and entered in the exception register. Beyond the description of what was waived, which single element most determines whether the register remains a control rather than becoming a list of permanent carve-outs?

options.text: An expiry date, after which the exception lapses unless it is re-argued and re-approved.
The approver's job title and delegated authority limit, with the date on which the waiver was signed off.
A severity rating derived from the specific policy clause that was waived.
A hyperlink to the governance forum minutes and the paper tabled when the exception was discussed.

explanation.correct: Exceptions are granted against a set of conditions that hold at a moment in time — a deadline, a missing capability, a vendor limitation. Those conditions change; the exception does not, unless something forces it to be revisited. An expiry date is the only field that makes lapse the default and continuation the thing requiring effort. Without it, an exception register grows monotonically and, after two or three years, describes the organisation's actual operating state rather than a set of deviations from it.

distractors.B: Approver and date establish who authorised the deviation and are needed for audit, but they are backward-looking. They tell you how the exception came to exist; they do nothing to bring it to an end or to force a re-examination of the reasoning.
distractors.C: Severity helps prioritise which exceptions to review and how much compensating control to demand. It orders the queue but does not create the review event, so a high-severity exception with no expiry simply sits at the top of a list nobody works.
distractors.D: Traceability to the discussion supports an auditor reconstructing the decision. It adds no forcing function, and in practice the minutes record the same conditions that the expiry date would have made the organisation retest.

explanation.concept: Every exception needs a stated end. Design exception workflows so that expiry is automatic and renewal requires positive action, with an owner and a compensating control named. A register whose entries never expire is documentation of drift, not governance of it.
explanation.tip: In governance items, prefer the option that creates a forcing function over the options that improve record-keeping. Ask which field, if missing, lets the entry live forever.

topic: Restoring compliance with a bypassed AI approval gate
stem: A UK insurer requires every AI use case to pass a governance review board that meets monthly; median time from submission to decision is eleven weeks. Nine use cases went through the board last year. Internal audit then found twenty-three AI use cases running in production that never did — almost all of them small internal tools built by analysts, such as summarising broker emails or drafting internal meeting notes. The CRO wants the bypass rate down. Which change is most likely to achieve that?

options.text: Make bypassing the board a disciplinary matter: circulate the audit findings to every line manager, require an explanation for each of the twenty-three cases, and reflect repeat bypasses in individual performance objectives.
Move the board to a fortnightly cadence and add reviewers drawn from each business line so that decision throughput roughly doubles without changing the review criteria.
Instruct the platform team to refuse any deployment request that does not quote a board approval reference, and withdraw the twenty-three unapproved tools until each has been reviewed.

Introduce risk tiering with a catalogue of pre-approved patterns: cases that match a documented low-risk pattern self-register and are cleared by the platform team in days, and only cases outside the catalogue reach the board.

explanation.correct: The bypass is a rational response to a gate priced far above the risk it is pricing. Eleven weeks of review to approve a meeting-notes summariser is a cost no analyst will pay, so they route around it. Twenty-three of twenty-three non-compliant cases being low-risk internal tools is the diagnostic detail: the gate has one setting and the estate has two populations. Risk tiering with a pre-approved pattern catalogue makes the compliant path the cheapest path for the common case, which is the only durable way to raise compliance, and preserves full scrutiny for the cases that warrant it.

distractors.A: Enforcement without a viable compliant route pushes the activity further underground rather than into the process. Analysts who face an eleven-week queue and a disciplinary risk will stop telling anyone, which converts a visibility problem into an invisible one.
distractors.B: Doubling throughput on a queue with an eleven-week median still leaves weeks of latency, and it applies the same depth of review to a broker-email summariser as to a pricing model. The mismatch between review cost and risk is untouched.
distractors.C: A deployment chokepoint is a genuinely useful mechanism and belongs in the eventual design, but on its own it funnels all twenty-three cases into the same eleven-week queue and takes working tools out of service while they wait. It enforces a gate that is still mispriced.

explanation.concept: A governance gate that costs more than the risk it manages will be bypassed, and the bypass rate is a measurement of the gate's design, not of staff discipline. Tier by risk and build a paved road so that the lowest-risk majority has a fast, sanctioned path.
explanation.tip: When a stem tells you what kind of use cases bypassed the gate, that characterisation is the clue. A population of uniformly low-risk violations points at proportionality, not at enforcement.

topic: First action after an AI incident with mutable configuration
stem: A New Zealand health insurer's member-facing Claude assistant told a member that a treatment was covered when it was not; the member proceeded and the resulting claim was declined. The complaint reached the AI incident channel at 09:10. Prompt templates live in a repository, but production overrides are applied through an operations console that keeps no change history; conversation logs are retained for thirty days. The on-call engineer disabled the assistant with its feature flag at 09:15 and now wants to correct the coverage wording so it can be re-enabled before the afternoon peak. As incident lead, what should happen first?

options.text: Approve the prompt correction and re-enable the assistant before the afternoon peak, then reconstruct the original configuration from the repository's commit history during the postmortem.

Capture the configuration that was in force during the member's conversation — console overrides, model version, retrieved documents, flag state — and export the affected transcripts before anything is changed.
Notify the regulator's incident line now, on the basis that a member has suffered financial detriment as a direct result of an automated communication the insurer itself published to them.
Raise conversation-log retention across the platform from thirty days to seven years, so the evidence supporting this complaint cannot age out during a lengthy dispute.

explanation.correct: Two details in the stem make this urgent rather than procedural: the console keeps no history, and the assistant is already off, so nothing is being made worse by waiting. The moment someone edits the override, the only copy of what the system was actually doing when it misinformed the member is destroyed — and this is a case that will be reconstructed later by a complaints handler, possibly a regulator, and possibly a court. Ongoing harm was stopped at 09:15; the next obligation is to freeze the evidence before remediation overwrites it.

distractors.A: The repository holds the templates, not the console overrides that were actually in force. Reconstructing from the repository would produce a confident but wrong account of what the member was told and why, which is worse than having no account.
distractors.C: External notification may well follow, but it is a decision for legal and the accountable executive against the organisation's own criteria, and it should be made on the basis of established facts. An incident lead escalating externally before the evidence is even secured has nothing accurate to report.
distractors.D: Extending retention is a sensible remediation item and the affected transcripts are still inside the window, so nothing is lost by doing it later. It also does nothing to preserve the console configuration, which is the artefact genuinely at risk.

explanation.concept: In an AI incident, the reproducible unit is the full request context — prompt, overrides, model version, retrieved content, flags, tool results — and much of it lives in places that are mutable and unversioned. Once harm is stopped, snapshot state before you fix anything.
explanation.tip: A stem that mentions a console with no change history is telling you the evidence is one edit away from gone. Kill switch first, snapshot second, fix third.

topic: AI-specific gaps in a completed SaaS vendor assessment
stem: A Canadian benefits administrator is onboarding a claims-triage product from a small software vendor. The product is built on a hosted Claude deployment and decides which claims go to a fast-track path and which go to manual assessment. The security team has completed its standard SaaS assessment: independent security attestation reviewed, penetration-test summary read, encryption and single sign-on confirmed, hosting region verified. The AI governance lead says the assessment is incomplete. Which TWO gaps are most material given what this product does? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Whether the contract governs how submitted claim data may be reused — in particular retention and use for improving the vendor's own product — and how those terms flow through to the vendor's model provider.
Whether the vendor's engineering team uses an AI coding assistant internally, which determines how much of the product's source code was machine-generated and therefore how much of it was reviewed.

Whether the vendor will notify the administrator and allow re-testing before changing the underlying model or the triage prompts, since the fast-track behaviour can shift with no change on the administrator's side.
Whether the vendor can produce per-request cost breakdowns so that the administrator can forecast variable spend and hold the contract inside its approved technology budget.
Whether the vendor's hosting region matches the administrator's primary operating region, so that claim data does not traverse jurisdictions during normal processing.

explanation.correct: A standard SaaS assessment answers whether the vendor can be trusted to hold data securely. It does not answer the two questions that are specific to buying an AI product. The first is data reuse: whether claim data submitted for triage can be retained or used to improve the vendor's product, and whether the vendor's own model provider is bound to the same terms — a subprocessor chain the administrator has not looked at. The second is behavioural change control: this product makes a decision, and the model or prompts behind that decision can be swapped by the vendor at any time, changing outcomes with no deployment on the administrator's side and no signal that anything happened.

distractors.B: How the vendor writes its own code is a software assurance question already partly addressed by the penetration test and any code-quality terms. It has no bearing on how the product treats claim data or on whether its triage behaviour is stable.
distractors.D: Cost forecasting is a commercial requirement, not a risk one. It belongs in the contract negotiation but does not change the administrator's exposure if triage behaviour drifts or if claim data is reused.
distractors.E: The stem states that hosting region has already been verified as part of the completed security assessment. Re-raising a closed item does not fill a gap, and residency alone would not address either of the AI-specific exposures.

explanation.concept: Vendor AI risk assessment extends security due diligence with two questions security assessments do not ask: what happens to the data you send, all the way down the subprocessor chain; and what happens when the vendor changes the model or prompts underneath you. Both need contractual answers, not verbal ones.
explanation.tip: In multi-select vendor items, discard any option the stem has already told you is complete, and any option that is commercial rather than risk-based. That usually leaves exactly the number of keys.

topic: Leading content of an AI risk report to a board committee
stem: An AI risk report is going to a board audit committee whose remit is assurance over the control environment rather than delivery oversight. What should the report lead with?

options.text: Per-system quality metrics for each production deployment, including evaluation pass rates and measured error rates broken down by use case.
A narrative of the year's AI investment, with spend attributed by business unit and the efficiency savings projected against each programme.
Coverage and exceptions: how much of the AI estate is registered and assessed, which risk acceptances are open, who owns them, and when they expire.
An architecture overview of the AI platform showing the gateway, guardrail and logging components and the vendors supplying each of them.

explanation.correct: An audit committee is asking one question in several forms: is the control environment working, and what do we not know? Coverage answers the second half — an estate that is 60% registered means 40% of the exposure is undescribed, which is the single most decision-relevant number available. Open exceptions with owners and expiry dates answer the first half by showing where the organisation has knowingly accepted risk and whether those acceptances are being retired. Both are things the committee can act on: demand coverage, challenge an acceptance, or escalate an owner.

distractors.A: Quality metrics are the right report for a product or engineering forum. A board committee cannot calibrate an evaluation pass rate, cannot compare it across use cases, and has no lever to pull in response to one; it produces the appearance of oversight without the substance.
distractors.B: Investment and benefit belong to the board's strategy or finance discussion. Presenting them to an audit committee frames AI as a value question at the exact moment the committee is trying to form a view on whether the risk is controlled.
distractors.D: Platform architecture describes the machinery of control rather than its effectiveness. A committee shown a clean diagram may reasonably conclude the estate is covered by it, which is precisely the inference coverage data would contradict.

explanation.concept: Board-level AI reporting is about completeness and accepted risk, not model performance. Lead with what proportion of the estate is known and assessed, what has been formally accepted as an exception, who owns each acceptance, and when it expires — figures a committee can question and act on.
explanation.tip: Match the artefact to the forum's remit. Audit committee means assurance and coverage; strategy committee means value and roadmap; engineering forum means metrics.

topic: Making an AI register reconcile against production reality
stem: An Australian state transport agency keeps its AI register in a spreadsheet, updated when a project manager submits a form at design stage. An audit found that 40% of register entries describe systems that were never built or have since been retired, and that three systems currently in production are absent from it. All Claude access within the agency runs through a central gateway that issues per-application credentials. Which change would make the register reliable?

options.text: Require project managers to re-confirm each of their register entries every quarter, with the delivery office chasing non-responses, escalating outstanding ones to the responsible director, and reporting completion rates.

Move the register out of the spreadsheet into the agency's configuration management database so entries inherit the change-management, ownership and approval workflow already applied to other IT assets.

Make credential issuance the registration event and reconcile the register against live gateway credentials on a schedule: no credential without an entry, and any credential with no matching entry or no traffic is flagged.
Shift the registration point from design stage to go-live, so that entries describe systems that actually reached production rather than proposals that may never be funded.

explanation.correct: The register has both error directions — entries with no system and systems with no entry — which means it needs a source of truth it can be checked against, not just a better submission moment. The gateway already is that source of truth: nothing reaches Claude without a credential. Binding issuance to registration prevents the missing-entry direction structurally, and scheduled reconciliation against live credentials and their traffic catches the stale-entry direction, because a retired system's credential either disappears or goes quiet. That converts the register from a self-reported document into a reconciled one.

distractors.A: Quarterly attestation is the control that already failed, run more often. It relies on project managers remembering systems they no longer own, and the audit found entries for systems that were never built — precisely the kind of thing nobody feels ownership to correct.
distractors.B: Better tooling and workflow improve the quality of what is entered but not the completeness of what gets entered at all. The three unlisted production systems would be equally absent from a configuration management database, because nothing forces their appearance.
distractors.D: Registering at go-live fixes the phantom-project half of the problem and is a real improvement. It still depends on someone choosing to register, so the three unlisted systems could recur, and it does nothing about entries that go stale after retirement.

explanation.concept: An inventory is only as good as the chokepoint it is reconciled against. Find the technical control every AI system must pass through — gateway credentials, service accounts, network egress — make passage conditional on registration, and reconcile both directions on a schedule.
explanation.tip: When a stem reports errors in both directions, the answer must address both. Options that only improve the intake moment leave stale entries untouched.

topic: Why a mandatory human approval step is not a control
stem: A Kenyan microfinance lender uses Claude to draft explanations for declined credit applications. Policy requires a loan officer to review and approve each draft before it is sent, and that approval is the lender's accountability record for the decline communication. Officers handle around 180 drafts per shift; the review screen shows the drafted text and an Approve button; median time between opening a draft and approving it is four seconds; the override rate is 0.3%. Internal audit concludes the review is not a control. What is the strongest basis for that conclusion?

options.text: The reviewer is shown neither the applicant's data nor the policy rule behind the decision, and has neither the time nor the information to form an independent view, so the approval records assent rather than judgement.
The override rate is implausibly low; a review that is genuinely functioning would be expected to disagree with the model on a materially larger share of cases than three in every thousand.
The approval is recorded against an individual loan officer rather than against the credit committee that owns the decline policy and should therefore own its communication.

Reviewing every single draft does not scale at 180 per shift; the lender should replace it with a weekly sample sized to a documented confidence level and reported to the operations quality forum, so that officers examine fewer cases properly.

explanation.correct: A human step is a control only if the human can actually reach a different conclusion. Three facts in the stem say this one cannot: the screen shows the output but not the applicant data or the policy rule, so there is nothing to check the draft against; four seconds is not enough to read the draft, let alone evaluate it; and the interface offers approval as the only visible action. The officer is supplying a signature, and the lender has built its accountability record on that signature. The low override rate is a symptom of these conditions, not the finding itself.

distractors.B: Override rate is evidence, not a basis. A low rate is equally consistent with a model that is genuinely accurate on this task, so an audit finding resting on it alone would collapse the moment the team produced accuracy data. Reasoning from the rate rather than from the reviewer's conditions is the trap here.
distractors.C: Recording approval against a named individual is correct design — it is what makes the record accountable at all. A committee cannot approve 180 items a shift, and moving the record to a body would weaken accountability rather than strengthen it.
distractors.D: Sampling is a legitimate design for quality assurance, but it does not follow from this finding and it would not fix it. A sampled review conducted under the same four-second, no-context conditions is a smaller quantity of the same non-control.

explanation.concept: Human-in-the-loop is a control only when the reviewer has the information to judge, the time to use it, and a real path to override. Test any human step against those three conditions; if any is missing, the organisation has bought an accountability record rather than an actual review.
explanation.tip: When a stem gives you a median review time in seconds and a description of what the screen shows, it is handing you the answer. Do not be pulled to the override rate — it is the consequence, not the cause.

topic: Predictable effect of a ban with no sanctioned alternative
stem: An organisation issues a blanket prohibition on all use of external AI tools and provides no sanctioned internal alternative. What is the most predictable governance consequence?

options.text: Use continues on personal devices and personal accounts, outside the organisation's logging, contracts and discovery.
Use falls close to zero, because most staff will not knowingly breach an explicit written prohibition from their employer.
Vendors begin approaching procurement directly, shifting the organisation's exposure into the contracted and reviewable supply chain.
Approved projects stall while the policy is clarified, delaying the organisation's technology roadmap by a quarter or more.

explanation.correct: Prohibition changes where an activity happens far more reliably than whether it happens. Staff under delivery pressure who have found a tool useful do not stop; they move to a channel the employer cannot see — a personal phone, a personal account, a free tier paid for by nobody. The organisation loses the three things it most needs: logs of what data left, a contract governing how that data is used, and any prospect of discovering the use during an assessment. The exposure is unchanged and the visibility is worse.

distractors.B: This assumes compliance is driven by the existence of a rule. In practice compliance is driven by the cost of the compliant path, and when that path does not exist the rule mainly filters out the people who would have told you.
distractors.C: Procurement-led adoption is what happens when there is a sanctioned route to fund and buy tools. A blanket ban removes that route, so vendors are engaged informally by individual teams or not engaged at all.
distractors.D: Roadmap delay is a real cost of unclear policy, but the question asks about the governance consequence of the ban itself. Approved projects are not the exposure; the undeclared use the ban created is.

explanation.concept: Policy without a sanctioned path is a visibility reduction, not a risk reduction. Pair every prohibition with an approved alternative that is easier to use than the prohibited option, or accept that the behaviour continues where you cannot see it.
explanation.tip: Ask what the person under deadline pressure actually does next. Governance answers that assume people simply stop are almost always the distractor.

topic: Changes that re-trigger AI approval under a scaling standard
stem: A Singapore property manager runs a Claude assistant for tenants. Today it answers policy questions and drafts replies that a service coordinator reviews and sends. The governance standard requires a fresh risk assessment and re-approval whenever a system's risk profile changes materially. The team proposes several changes for next quarter. Which THREE require re-approval under that standard? (Choose THREE.)

options.text: The assistant will send its replies to tenants directly, with the coordinator reviewing a sample afterwards instead of every message beforehand.
The assistant will be given a tool that applies rent credits in the billing system up to a fixed per-case limit without a separate approval step.
The system prompt will be restructured to place the worked examples above the instructions, with the full evaluation suite rerun and the results unchanged.
Coverage will extend from the residential portfolio to the commercial one, whose lease terms, escalation clauses and dispute process differ and are absent from the current evaluation set.
Daily request volume is expected to roughly triple as more buildings are onboarded, with the same tasks, the same data sources and the same review step in place.

explanation.correct: Three dimensions change a risk profile: how much the system does without a human, what it can affect, and who or what it is applied to. Removing pre-send review moves the assistant from proposing to acting, and the sample-after-the-fact check catches errors only once tenants have already received them. Granting a tool that moves money in the billing system creates a new and irreversible class of consequence that the original assessment never contemplated. Extending to commercial leases applies an evaluated system to a domain it was not evaluated on, so the existing evidence no longer covers the population it is being used against.

distractors.C: Prompt restructuring is a change to the implementation, not to the risk profile, and the team has already produced the evidence that behaviour did not move. Requiring re-approval for changes that the evaluation suite shows to be behaviourally neutral is how organisations teach their teams to route around the gate.
distractors.E: Volume growth with identical task, data and oversight scales capacity and cost, not risk exposure per decision. It may warrant a load and rate-limit review, but nothing about what the system decides, what it can reach, or who reviews it has changed.

explanation.concept: Re-approval triggers should be defined by autonomy, blast radius, and population — the human step removed, a new action or system the model can affect, or a new user group or data domain outside the evaluated set. Throughput and behaviourally neutral refactors are not risk events.
explanation.tip: Volume increase is the classic decoy in responsible-scaling items. Scaling controls track what the system can do and to whom, not how often it does it.

topic: What an AI vendor assessment adds beyond security review
stem: What does an AI-specific third-party assessment need to establish that a standard vendor security assessment does not?

options.text: Whether the vendor encrypts customer data in transit and at rest and holds a current independent security attestation covering the service in scope.
Whether the vendor's availability commitments and support response times are sufficient to meet the buyer's own service obligations to its customers.
Whether the vendor maintains a documented business continuity and disaster recovery plan that has been tested within the last twelve months.
How inputs and outputs may be reused, whether the underlying model can change without notice, and how the vendor's own model provider is bound.

explanation.correct: Security assessments were designed for software that stores and processes data deterministically. Buying an AI-enabled product adds three exposures they do not probe. Data submitted as a prompt may be retained or used to improve the vendor's product unless the contract forbids it. The behaviour you accepted at onboarding can change silently when the vendor swaps a model or edits a prompt, with no release on your side. And the vendor is itself a customer of a model provider, so your data protections are only as strong as the terms flowing down that chain.

distractors.A: Encryption and independent attestation are the core of the standard assessment. They are necessary and they are already covered, which is exactly why they cannot be the incremental content of an AI-specific review.
distractors.B: Availability and support terms are ordinary service management. They matter for any supplier and are unaffected by whether the product uses a model, so they add nothing that is specific to AI risk.
distractors.C: Continuity and recovery testing is a resilience control found in every mature vendor assessment. It addresses the vendor going down, not the vendor changing model behaviour or reusing the data you sent it.

explanation.concept: AI vendor risk is data reuse, behavioural change control, and the subprocessor chain to the underlying model provider. Get all three into the contract as notice periods, reuse prohibitions and flow-down obligations; questionnaire answers about them are not enforceable.
explanation.tip: Recall items that contrast two assessment types are asking for the delta. Eliminate everything the baseline assessment already covers and one option is normally left standing.

topic: Judging whether a postmortem prevents recurrence
stem: A Polish marketplace ran a postmortem after its Claude-based listing moderation system approved a batch of counterfeit listings that stayed live for nine days. The document correctly traces the cause: the moderation evaluation suite is an optional step in the deployment pipeline, and the prompt change that caused the failure shipped without it. The three actions read: 'be more careful with prompt changes', 'consider adding evals to CI', and 'team to review the moderation policy'. The engineering director signed the postmortem and closed the incident. Which criticism is best supported?

options.text: The postmortem should have been written by a reviewer independent of the team that operates the system, because a team investigating its own failure will understate its contribution to it.
The postmortem should have identified which engineer approved the merge, so that accountability for the change that caused the exposure is recorded against a named person.
None of the actions is owned, dated or verifiable, and none makes the evaluation step mandatory, so the condition that produced the failure is still in place at closure.
Nine days of undetected exposure shows the incident's severity rating was set too low, and the correct remedy is to re-rate it before the incident can be closed.

explanation.correct: The analysis is right and the output is empty. An optional evaluation step in the pipeline is a precise, fixable condition, and the fix is one configuration change: make it required for this service. Instead the postmortem produced an exhortation, a suggestion hedged with 'consider', and an undated policy review — none assigned to a person, none with a completion state anyone can check. The incident was closed with the pipeline in exactly the state that allowed the failure, so the next prompt change can ship the same way.

distractors.A: Postmortems are written by the people closest to the system because they are the only ones who understand it in enough detail to find the real condition. Independence belongs in assurance over the process, not in authorship; imposing it typically produces shallower analysis and less candour.
distractors.B: The postmortem already identified a systemic cause: an optional gate. Naming the individual who merged adds no preventive value, and attaching blame to an engineer who used the pipeline as configured suppresses the reporting that makes future postmortems possible.
distractors.D: Severity governs the response during the incident. Re-rating a closed incident changes the record but not the pipeline; a correctly rated incident with unowned, unverifiable actions recurs just as readily as a misrated one.

explanation.concept: A postmortem is only complete when each action has a named owner, a date, and a state someone can verify — and when at least one action removes the condition that made the failure possible. 'Be more careful' is not an action; making an optional gate mandatory is.
explanation.tip: Read the action list before the analysis. Words like 'consider', 'review' and 'be more careful' with no owner mean the incident closed without changing anything, whatever the root-cause section says.

topic: Controlling silent model changes inside a purchased product
stem: A Chilean payments company embeds a third-party dispute-summarisation service in its operations console. Two weeks after a routine vendor release, summaries began omitting the chargeback reason code that the operations team relies on to route cases; the vendor confirmed it had moved to a different model tier. The contract covers security, availability and support but says nothing about model changes. The company's governance standard requires material changes to be assessed before they take effect. Which combination of contractual and operational change addresses this class of failure?

options.text: A contractual requirement that the vendor pin one named model version for the life of the agreement, so the behaviour tested at onboarding is the behaviour that continues to be delivered.

A change-notification and regression window in the contract — advance notice of model or prompt changes plus time to run the company's own acceptance tests — backed by running that test set against the vendor on a schedule.
An availability and accuracy service level with financial credits attached to each breach, so that the vendor carries the cost of degraded summaries and has a direct incentive to avoid causing them.

Rebuild the summarisation in-house on the company's own Claude deployment, retiring the third-party service at the next renewal and giving the operations team direct control over model version, prompt content, release timing and the summary template.

explanation.correct: The failure was silent and behavioural: nothing broke, nothing alerted, and the company only learned of the change by noticing degraded routing weeks later. Fixing that class needs both halves. The contractual half converts a silent change into a notified one and buys a window before it takes effect. The operational half is the company's own acceptance test set, run on a schedule rather than only at onboarding — because notice is worthless without the ability to detect whether the new behaviour still meets the requirement, and because it also catches changes the vendor forgets to notify.

distractors.A: Indefinite version pinning is rarely obtainable from a product vendor and is a poor goal even when it is. It blocks security and quality improvements, and it eventually collides with upstream deprecation, at which point the company faces the same untested change with no process for it.
distractors.C: Credits compensate after the harm, which here was cases routed to the wrong queue for two weeks. Accuracy is also extremely hard to define contractually for generative summaries, so the clause tends to be either unmeasurable or narrow enough to miss what actually went wrong.
distractors.D: Insourcing solves this instance at considerable cost and leaves the general problem untouched, since the company will still buy other AI-enabled products. It also trades vendor change risk for the full build, evaluation and operating burden of the capability.

explanation.concept: When you buy AI capability, you are buying behaviour that the vendor can change without deploying anything to you. Require notice and a regression window contractually, and hold your own acceptance test set that you run against the vendor periodically rather than only at onboarding.
explanation.tip: For third-party AI risk, look for the answer with both a contractual term and a detection mechanism. Contract-only options assume the vendor always tells you; detection-only options let the change land first.

topic: When rollback criteria for a staged AI rollout are set
stem: In a staged rollout of an AI system from pilot to full production, when should the criteria for halting or rolling back be defined?

options.text: After the first stage, once real production data has shown what normal behaviour for this system actually looks like.
Before the first stage begins, as part of the approval to proceed to that stage.
At each stage gate, by whichever team is operating the system during that quarter.
Only if an incident occurs, so that the criteria are grounded in the failure that was actually observed.

explanation.correct: Rollback criteria written after the system is live are written by people who now have sunk cost, a launch date, and a stakeholder expecting the next stage. Committing to them as a condition of approval — before anyone is invested in the outcome — is what makes them capable of being invoked. It also forces the approving body to be explicit about what level of harm or error would be unacceptable, which is a materially different and more useful conversation than approving in the abstract.

distractors.A: Waiting for baseline data sounds rigorous and is how thresholds for routine monitoring alerts get tuned. For a stop decision it inverts the incentive: the criteria are now set by people who have already launched and who will be judged on whether the rollout continues.
distractors.C: Per-gate definition by the operating team makes the standard drift with team composition and pressure, and produces no comparability between stages. The point of pre-committed criteria is that they are stable and were agreed by someone other than the people under delivery pressure.
distractors.D: Defining criteria only after an incident means the first failure has no threshold at all, so the argument about whether it is bad enough to stop happens during the incident, when it is least likely to be decided well.

explanation.concept: Pre-commit stop conditions before each stage of a rollout, as part of the approval. Criteria decided in advance by people with no stake in continuing are the only ones that reliably survive contact with a launch commitment.
explanation.tip: Responsible-scaling items reward pre-commitment. If one option sets the exit criteria before entry and the others set them later, that is nearly always the key.

topic: Converting an AI use attestation into an enforceable control
stem: A Brazilian retailer's AI usage policy prohibits placing customer personal data into any AI tool. Enforcement consists of a mandatory annual training module and a signed attestation. Six months on, a data-loss review finds customer records in prompts sent to the sanctioned internal Claude gateway and in traffic to two external consumer AI products. The head of data protection wants enforcement that does not depend on staff remembering the rule. Which TWO changes achieve that? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Apply the existing egress data-loss rules to AI endpoints and to the internal gateway's request bodies, so a prompt carrying customer data is blocked or masked at submission rather than found in a later review.
Increase the training module from annual to quarterly and add a scored assessment that staff must pass before their gateway credentials are renewed for the following period.
Route all corporate access to external AI products through the same gateway, or block direct access, so there is a single enforcement point at which the policy can actually be applied.
Add a full-width warning banner to the gateway interface restating the prohibition and the disciplinary consequences at the start of every session a user opens.
Require each business unit head to countersign the attestation on behalf of their team, raising the level of management at which the existing commitment is made.

explanation.correct: A control acts on the action itself. Applying data-loss inspection to AI traffic and to the gateway's request bodies means a prompt containing customer data is stopped or masked at the moment of submission — no employee decision is required for the policy to hold. That only works where traffic is visible, and the review found data going to two external products the gateway never sees, so the second change is to make the gateway the sole route for corporate AI access. Together they create a single inspected chokepoint; either alone leaves an uncontrolled path or an uninspected one.

distractors.B: More frequent training with a test still relies on the employee recalling and applying the rule at the moment of a copy-paste under deadline pressure. It raises awareness and it strengthens the disciplinary case afterwards, but nothing about it prevents or detects the act.
distractors.D: Banner warnings are habituated away within days and are ignored by exactly the population that most needs them. They are a nudge in the interface, not an enforcement mechanism, and they cover only the gateway that is already the more controlled path.
distractors.E: Countersignature redistributes accountability for the commitment without changing anything about how the commitment is kept. A business unit head signing for a team has no more visibility into individual prompt content than the individuals had.

explanation.concept: A requirement enforced only by training and attestation is not a control — it is an expectation with an audit trail. Convert it by routing the activity through a chokepoint you control and inspecting or blocking at that point, so compliance is the default rather than a choice.
explanation.tip: Score each option by asking whether it still works if every employee forgets the policy entirely. Options that fail that test are awareness measures, however often they are repeated.
